bottom: Acton's money is the reverse of her opponent's. She has many donors, mostly in Ohio, and few large checks. Her biggest institutional backers are the Ohio Democratic Party and organized labor. In September 2026 she raised slightly more than $6 million against Vivek Ramaswamy's just over $3 million. Even so, her total donations since entering the race were still about $5 million short of the more than $36 million Ramaswamy has put in himself, per the Ohio Capital Journal on October 13, 2026, https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2026/10/13/ramaswamy-loans-campaign-5-million-more-as-acton-outpaces-him-with-donors/.
Three interests combine real money with a decision she would control:

**Labor unions.** The Ohio Federation of Teachers, the UAW, IBEW, the bricklayers and the firefighters back her. She has promised to keep Ohio from becoming a right to work state and to resist SB 5 style limits on bargaining. IBEW also put $1 million into the Democratic Governors Association's Ohio committee.

**The Ohio Democratic Party and the DGA.** The party gave $125,000 through 2025 and $232,000 in September 2026. The DGA built a state committee, Ohioans For Lower Costs, and planned a $9.4 million campaign.

Ramaswamy is the most expensive candidate in Ohio history and the money comes from three places: his own fortune, a federal super PAC fed by a handful of billionaires, and a donor base that is broad but thin in Ohio. He has committed more than $36 million of his own money as loans he can repay from donor funds, per the Ohio Capital Journal on October 13, 2026, https://ohiocapitaljournal.com/2026/10/13/ramaswamy-loans-campaign-5-million-more-as-acton-outpaces-him-with-donors/. V-PAC: Victors Not Victims, FEC ID C00892919, has taken at least $30 million from Jeff Yass alone, per Signal Ohio on August 27, 2026, https://signalohio.org/billionaire-jeff-yass-ohio-governor-race-november-election-2026/.
Four interests have both real money in and a dated decision on the next governor's desk:

**Billionaire tax cut donors.** Yass, Elon Musk, Ratmir Timashev, Ross Stevens and Bill Ackman want his income tax phase out, which starts with repealing the capital gains tax. That fight is the 2027 budget.

**Data center and power interests.** He has promised a day one order halting new data center approvals, which cuts against some V-PAC donors. AEP's PAC and the submetering industry gave to his campaign. He controls PUCO and Power Siting Board seats.

D.t: Amy Acton leads by 4.2 in the forecast and wins 79% of simulations. The cushion is about 202,144 votes; a one point swing is about 23,894 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +2.4 and D +11.0. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +4.0. Your best recent poll is Suffolk University/USA TODAY Network at D +7.3; your worst is ActiVote at R +2.8. 15 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Franklin, a projected net 236,996 votes; Cuyahoga, a projected net 233,477 votes; Hamilton, a projected net 98,364 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Montgomery, D +11.7, 4.5% of the vote; Stark, R +5.6, 3.2% of the vote; Lorain, D +7.1, 2.7% of the vote; Delaware, D +1.7, 2.3% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Amy Acton runs furthest behind in Greene, Delaware, Clermont. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 43 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.08 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 67% of voters, 48 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.37 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 55 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Amy Acton: Immigration voters 22 to 74, Small counties 29 to 68, Midsize counties 43 to 54. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$3.6M cash against $2.4M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Activity: 11 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.

R.t: Vivek Ramaswamy trails by 4.2 and wins 21% of simulations. Closing it takes about 101,072 voters switching sides, or 202,144 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +11.0 and R +2.4. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +4.0. Your best recent poll is ActiVote at R +2.8; your worst is Suffolk University/USA TODAY Network at D +7.3. 15 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Clermont, a projected net 25,131 votes; Warren, a projected net 22,604 votes; Butler, a projected net 21,983 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Montgomery, D +11.7, 4.5% of the vote; Stark, R +5.6, 3.2% of the vote; Lorain, D +7.1, 2.7% of the vote; Delaware, D +1.7, 2.3% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Vivek Ramaswamy runs furthest behind in Clark, Mahoning, Portage. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 82% of voters, 54 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.08 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 67% of voters, 48 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.37 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 40 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Vivek Ramaswamy: Black voters 9 to 88, Asian and other voters 22 to 74, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 30 to 67. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.4M cash against $3.6M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

media.what: On a livestream after Ramaswamy criticized him at AmericaFest, said he would work against Ramaswamy's election and called it the only 2026 race he cares about.
After Ramaswamy won the GOP primary, urged followers on his livestream to vote for Democrat Amy Acton as a protest vote or stay home.
As Ohio early voting opened, posted repeated calls on X for followers to vote for Acton; one post drew about 2 million views.
Posted an unverified, unsourced claim about Amy Acton's conduct at an event; the Ohio Republican Party's account amplified it and credited her.
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the Ohio governor race from Leans Republican to Toss-up.
Said the Ohio governor race has flipped to Amy Acton, up 4, and called Ramaswamy's standing with independents the worst this century.
Interviewed Vivek Ramaswamy on All Sides about the gas tax holiday, property taxes and Amy Acton's refusal to debate.
Anchored The 11th Hour live from Columbus covering the Ohio governor and Senate races.
Called Ramaswamy's ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother indefensible and predicted it will blow up in their face.
On NewsNight called the Ramaswamy ad risky and said launching it late was not reassuring for the campaign.
Called Ramaswamy's Acton mother ad extremely risky and asked if it signals trouble for his campaign.
Called the Ramaswamy ad unbelievably disgusting and said he would no longer vote for Ramaswamy.
